scope: Original school-taught Chemistry mock drawings: E/Z stereoisomers, optical isomerism, aldehyde/ketone structure comparison and ester structure; manually assessed
notes: All diagrams are hypothetical exam drawings, with no laboratory use, sourcing or preparation instructions. Every marking point is self-reviewed, not inferred from image text matching.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.series: Original AQA-style Organic Chemistry Drawing Practice
questions.question: Draw both enantiomers of butan-2-ol
questions.prompt: Draw a pair of three-dimensional, non-superimposable mirror-image structures of butan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, using solid wedges and dashed bonds at the chiral carbon. Identify the chiral centre. Use the sketch/photo and manual mark-point checker: this answer requires a drawing. [4 marks]
markPoints: The second carbon is correctly identified as the stereogenic (chiral) centre.
Each structure attaches the four different groups OH, H, CH₃ and CH₂CH₃ to that carbon.
The 3D wedge/dashed-bond arrangement is internally consistent and stereochemically possible in both drawings.
The second structure is the non-superimposable mirror image of the first, with opposite configuration rather than a mere rotation.
questions.modelAnswer: Butan-2-ol has one chiral carbon, C2, bonded to H, OH, CH₃ and CH₂CH₃. Draw tetrahedral wedge/dash structures with all four groups correctly connected, then invert the stereochemistry at C2 to show the enantiomer. Merely swapping the two drawings on the page or rotating one does not create a different enantiomer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.series: Original AQA-style Organic Chemistry Drawing Practice
questions.question: Draw and distinguish propanal and propanone
questions.prompt: Draw clear displayed or unambiguous structural formulas of propanal and propanone, both with molecular formula C₃H₆O. Label the C=O group in each and explain which is an aldehyde and which is a ketone. Use manual diagram review for your four marking points. [4 marks]
markPoints: Propanal is correctly drawn as CH₃CH₂C(=O)H (CH₃CH₂CHO), with a terminal carbonyl group.
Propanone is correctly drawn as CH₃C(=O)CH₃, with the carbonyl carbon between two carbon groups.
The C=O carbonyl group and double bond are correctly shown and labelled in both structures.
Propanal is identified as an aldehyde (carbonyl carbon bonded to H), whereas propanone is identified as a ketone (carbonyl carbon bonded to two C groups).
questions.modelAnswer: Propanal: CH₃–CH₂–C(=O)–H, an aldehyde with the carbonyl carbon at the chain end and bonded to hydrogen. Propanone: CH₃–C(=O)–CH₃, a ketone whose carbonyl carbon is bonded to two methyl groups. Both have a C=O double bond but different functional-group environments.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.series: Original AQA-style Organic Chemistry Drawing Practice
questions.question: Draw both E and Z isomers of but-2-ene
questions.prompt: Draw and label the two geometrical stereoisomers of but-2-ene, CH₃CH=CHCH₃. Show the arrangement of the methyl and hydrogen groups around the C=C bond clearly, using displayed or unambiguous structural drawings. Explain briefly why these are distinct isomers. Review your drawings manually. [4 marks]
markPoints: Both drawn structures have the correct but-2-ene connectivity, CH₃–CH=CH–CH₃, with a hydrogen and methyl group on each double-bond carbon.
The Z isomer has the two higher-priority methyl groups on the same side of the C=C bond.
The E isomer has the two higher-priority methyl groups on opposite sides of the C=C bond.
Both structures are correctly labelled E/Z and recognise restricted rotation around the carbon–carbon double bond.
questions.modelAnswer: Draw the planar carbon–carbon double bond with CH₃ and H attached to each double-bonded carbon. Z-but-2-ene has the CH₃ groups on the same side; E-but-2-ene has the CH₃ groups on opposite sides. Distinct E/Z configurations exist because rotation around the double bond is restricted.

questions.question: Draw and label ethyl propanoate
questions.prompt: Draw a clear displayed or unambiguous structural formula of ETHYL PROPANOATE and identify its ester linkage. On the same drawing label which part comes from the propanoic acid and which part from the ethanol. No preparation conditions are required. Review the structure manually. [4 marks]
markPoints: Correct complete connectivity is drawn as CH₃CH₂–C(=O)–O–CH₂CH₃.
The carbonyl O is double-bonded to the acid-derived carbon; the adjacent ether-like O is single-bonded to the carbonyl C.
The propanoate (acid-derived) section is correctly indicated as CH₃CH₂C(=O)O–.
The ethyl (alcohol-derived) section is correctly indicated as –CH₂CH₃ attached through the ester oxygen, not directly to carbonyl carbon.
questions.modelAnswer: The formula is CH₃CH₂C(=O)OCH₂CH₃. The CH₃CH₂C(=O)O– group derives from propanoic acid; the –CH₂CH₃ attached to the single-bonded oxygen derives from ethanol. The –C(=O)–O– group is the ester linkage, not an ether or a ketone.
